thread.title: Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years, and the owner of Dairy Queen, Edina Realty led the way

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years, and the owner of Dairy Queen, Edina Realty led the way
text: – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Aug 31, 2018, 2:57pm CDT U.S. companies rebounded from a lackluster showing in the first quarter of the year with a surge in profits that's expected to fuel even more economic growth in the months ahead. The Commerce Department reported this week that after-tax profits among U.S. companies jumped 16.1 percent on a year-over-year during the quarter that ended June 30, qualifying as the largest such increase since 2012. The boom was especially pronounced in the banking industry, which pocketed more after-tax profits than any other sector in Q2. Among U.S. financial companies, profits increased $16.8 billion in the second quarter, in contrast to a decrease of $9.3 billion in the first quarter. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department reported that profits at non-financial corporations increased $63.6 billion, compared with an increase of $32.3 billion. A Business Journals analysis of more than 3,000 publicly traded companies found that the electronics components sector saw the largest profit gains over the same period in 2017. The sector reported $15.9 billion in profit during the second quarter — $8.5 billion more than what it earned during the year-earlier period. Warren Buffett 's Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) posted the largest quarterly profit of any public company in the second quarter, and it also posted the strongest year-over-year gain. The Omaha, Nebraska-based investment company netted $12 billion last quarter, marking a $7.8 billion increase over 2017's corresponding period. Berkshire owns Edina-based International Dairy Queen Inc., the ice cream-centered restaurant chain, and Minneapolis-based HomeServices of America, which runs Edina Realty in Minnesota as well as multiple other residential realty brokerage brands throughout the United States. Berkshire’s success narrowly beat the world’s first trillion-dollar company. Apple’s (Nasdaq: AAPL) second-quarter profits topped $11.5 billion, a $2.8 billion improvement from a year earlier. Rounding out the top five were Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT), which earned $8.9 billion (up $804 million); JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), with $8.3 billion (up $1.3 billion); and Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), with $6.9 billion (up $1.7 billion).
